frase_gancho.texto: Supernatural animals, almost always felines, that dominate people.

puente_narrativo.texto: Continue along your route: the story of the felines and the rain goes on up the slope.

guion_corto.texto: There are reliefs where an enormous animal dominates a person. The great reliefs on the boulders at the base of the hill speak of mythology and ritual. Most of them show supernatural animals dominating people. Grove cites Monuments Three, Four, Five and Thirty-One as examples. In almost every case they are felines. These rocks were not carved on a building, but on natural stones that were already there, scattered at the base of the hill. They were natural, and they were there before anyone carved them. Perhaps that is why the scene seems to emerge from the earth itself. Do not settle on a single image: look at them as a group.

guion_largo.texto:
Some rocks were already important before anyone carved them. At the base of Cerro Chalcatzingo there are large natural boulders, scattered about, and several of them were turned into reliefs.

Grove explains that these great reliefs illustrate themes related to mythology and religious rituals. Most of them show supernatural animals dominating people. He cites Monuments Three, Four, Five and Thirty-One as examples. In almost every case they are felines.

We will not go into the fine detail of each one. The sources consulted do not allow us to say with certainty which is which, or how the figures are arranged. What you can see is the general idea: a supernatural being, almost always a feline, and people under its dominion.

A boulder is a large, loose rock, of the kind that stays on a hillside. These were not brought here: they were already there, and the sculptors worked on them. With that gesture they turned a landscape into a set of images.

Eulalia Guzmán documented, in nineteen thirty-four, a few stones, but very elaborate ones. Many more have been added since then. If you can, compare the size of each relief with that of your own body.

A clue to the history of each relief is given by its number. Monuments Three, Four and Five had already been excavated in nineteen seventy-two. Thirty-One is one of those registered later. The numbers help to follow the history of the discoveries, although they do not say when each one was carved.

Arqueología Mexicana gathers an idea that helps in reading these reliefs. In the code of meaning of that period, the mountain is the place where ancestors and supernatural beings dwell, and the cave is the entrance to their home. That magazine cites Chalcatzingo, along with Zohapilco, Teopantecuanitlán and El Manatí, as places where that element can be seen.

Compare this idea with what you saw on the terraces. There were stelae of elite individuals, some decapitated or buried. On the hill, the beings that dominate are supernatural, and the reliefs remain on their rock, unmutilated. Grove stresses that these themes vary according to place.

Stone also suffers. Grove, in the PARI journal, warns about the damage that acid rain does to the reliefs. That is why INAH has built roofs and walls to protect them. When you see these structures, remember that they are guarding something very old and very delicate.

And there is more. Among the reliefs at the base is the [Triad of the Felines](chz_14_triada_felinos), found only a few years ago. Grove says it is another example of supernatural felines.

To close, return to the idea of the walk. These reliefs stand several meters apart. They cannot be seen together. You have to walk from one to another, and in that walking the story comes together.

texto: Notice whether in each relief you see the person or the animal first
Look for the roofs and walls that protect the rock
Compare the size of the relief with your own body

texto.Support: large boulders at the base of the hill

texto.pregunta: Myth: The reliefs are decoration for a temple.
texto.respuesta: Reality: They are carved on natural boulders and on the rock of the hill; their themes are mythology and ritual.
